Actually phenyl with three OH substituents: C6H3(OH)3 = C6H3O3H3 = C6H6O3? Wait each OH adds O and H. Base phenyl C6H3 (since three positions have OH, three hydrogens left). So C6H3 + 3*(OH) = C6H3 + O3H3 = C6H6O3. So fragment formula C6H6O3.

Second fragment CC(O)CO: let's compute: CH3-CH(OH)-CH2OH => C3H8O2? Actually CH3 (C1 H3), CH(OH) (C1 H1 + OH adds O H), CH2OH (C1 H2 + OH adds O H). Total C3, H: 3+1+2 =6 plus two OH hydrogens =2 => total H8. O2. So C3H8O2.

Actually maybe the phenol is attached via carbon (C-O bond) to the propylene glycol carbon, not via condensation. That reduces H2 and O? Actually water removal removes O from one OH? Wait condensation of two alcohols forms ether and water: R-OH + R'-OH -> R-O-R' + H2O. So lose two H and one O. Starting total O5? Starting H14, lose 2 => H12, still too many (need H10). Need lose 4 H total. Could be two linkages? But only one connection likely.
